_comment: Every item that can sit in a satchel slot. CLAUDE.md: data that will clearly vary per item lives here, never in gameplay code. scripts/ui and autoload contain no item literals.
_comment_scope: MEADOWS_VERTICAL_SLICE.md M8 asks for a minimal starting set. Orbs and the small potion joined it when the opening gained Grandpa's parting gifts and orbs stopped being a placeholder counter in throw_aim.gd — they are real inventory now, spent from the satchel by every throw. Tools and cooked food are still M8/M9 and deliberately absent rather than stubbed.
_comment_heal: `heal` is what one use restores on a creature, in HP. Present only on consumables that heal; tunable.
_comment_revive: D40 (OF32, owner: 'Grandpa should give you revives at the beginning too'). `revive` is the fraction of max HP a Revive restores when used on a FAINTED creature (0.5 == half, tunable) -- creature_instance.gd's revive() reads it, not heal(). As of D40, `heal` items (potions) refuse a fainted creature outright instead of un-fainting it; `revive` items are the only thing that clears `fainted` outside of rest (home_recovery.gd/creature beds, which still heal_fully() -- that is rest, not a potion, and stays untouched).
_comment_stack: `stack` is the slot cap. GAME_DESIGN.md 19: slot + stack, NO weight limit — there is no `weight` key here and there must never be one.
_comment_fiber: Spelled `fiber`, matching MEADOWS_VERTICAL_SLICE.md section M8 AND the harvest data the gathering work will port from the pre-Godot prototype (git show c45dee5^:src/data/harvest.json), which drops wood, stone, fiber, berries and flint under exactly these ids. The id is what harvesting keys off, so it had to match one of them; it now matches both.
_comment_colour: `colour` is the slot tile's tint. Placeholder standing in for an icon, and sampled so four resources are told apart at a glance on a 7-inch screen rather than by reading four short words.
_comment_tools: R2.1. `gathered_with` on a resource names the tool id that gathers it at full amount; a resource with no `gathered_with` (berries) is never tool-gated. item_db.gd's harvest_yield() reads it: the right tool gives the harvest node's full amount, no tool gives a reduced bare-handed amount (BAREHANDED_FRACTION, tunable), and owning some other tool but not the right one gives nothing. Tools themselves are `kind: tool`, `stack: 1` — owned, not consumed. `hammer` and `fishing_rod` exist as items now per this task's own brief but gate nothing yet: the workbench/repair loop (R2.2) and fishing (unscheduled -- R7.6 was re-scoped off fishing and onto the berry farm) are what will read them. R7.6 added a sixth tool, `hoe`, and it is the first one that does NOT appear here: it gates TILLING, a preparation verb, not a gather, so it is named by scripts/world/farm_logic.gd::TILL_TOOL instead of by any resource's `gathered_with`. Berries are still the resource with no `gathered_with`, farmed ones included -- see docs/decisions/D50 for why that was kept deliberately rather than quietly changed the moment berries got a farm.
_comment_durability: R2.2. `durability` is the number of full-yield gathers a tool survives before it breaks (GAME_DESIGN.md 19: 'have durability', 'repair for free at appropriate station'). Tunable, same for all five for now. A broken tool (0 durability) stops counting as owned for item_db.gd's harvest_yield() gating until repaired -- inventory.gd tracks the current value per-slot, defaulting to this max when a slot carries no durability key of its own (so a freshly-added tool needs no special-cased add-time write). Only `axe`/`pickaxe`/`knife` actually lose durability today, from harvest_node.gd's gather loop; `hammer` and `fishing_rod` carry the field for GAME_DESIGN.md consistency but nothing damages them yet, matching R2.1's own precedent for those two.
_comment_satiety: D29. `satiety` is how much of player_vitals.gd's satiety meter one use restores (see data/config/vitals.json); `buff` is that same use's optional temporary buff, passed straight through to player_vitals.gd's eat() as-is: { id, stat, amount, duration_s }. Only berries carry it so far. Nothing calls eat() from an eating action yet -- that wiring lands with the HUD pass, per this task's brief.
_comment_creature_food: RG19-spec/D68. `creature_food` is what one use of this item does for a CREATURE's condition -- `nourishment` restores the fed meter (data/config/creature_condition.json), `happiness` is the mood a fed creature gains, and omitting `happiness` falls back to that file's own `on_feed`. It is a separate key from `satiety` on purpose: berries are both a player's snack and a team's dinner, and the two meters are tuned independently. An item with this key is offered to the party through the backpack's ordinary target picker, exactly as a tonic is.
_comment_tm: OF29 (owner: 'I can pick up a TM but it needs to go in my inventory and then I see it's stats and choose who to teach it to'). A `kind: "tm"` item is a teaching disc you carry: its id is EXACTLY the matching data/moves/tms.json id (that is the whole link between the two files -- tests/test_moves.gd asserts it both ways, so a TM item with no TM entry, or a TM entry with no item, fails the build). `move` names the data/moves/moves.json id it teaches and must match that TM entry's own `move_id`; the backpack detail view reads power/type/slot from move_db.gd and the compatibility list from tm_db.gd rather than duplicating either here. `stack: 1` because a TM is now CONSUMED on teach (owner-directed change to R4.4's never-consumed design) -- one disc teaches one creature, so a satchel slot holding 'a stack of TMs' would be a lie about what the player can actually do with it.
_comment_coin: D39 (OF31, owner: 'Make the villagers so I can trade with them'). The owner chose a simple coin currency, and `coin` is an ORDINARY item in this table for that reason -- it stacks in a satchel slot, shows in the backpack like everything else, saves through the same inventory array, and can be dropped in a death satchel. There is no wallet, no second store and no `coins` field on game_state, and there must never be one: the moment currency lives somewhere else, every screen that shows your things has to learn about it separately. `kind: currency` is descriptive only -- nothing branches on it (item_db.gd's only kind branch is `tool`), it exists so the backpack detail line can say what this is. Prices are NOT here: they are per-vendor and tunable, and live in data/config/trade.json.
_comment_icons: M-G groundwork. `icon` is a res:// path to a 64px Kenney Game Icons silhouette (see docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md's 'Item + shared UI icons' row for the per-item source mapping and its honest mismatches -- this pack has no literal axe/wood/flask glyphs, so several are the closest available stand-in, same convention as the map icons row). `description` is the fuller inventory-detail text; `blurb` stays as the shorter existing field, both kept side by side rather than one replacing the other. Joined with the UI icon-set vendoring pass in the same commit-to-be.
_comment_rootstone: SD18. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md 10: the first of the Meadows' two progression-tier materials, above baseline wood/stone/fiber/berries. `gathered_with: pickaxe` matches the existing stone convention -- Rootstone is a harder seam, not a different gathering verb. SD16 (a sibling item, quarry harvest nodes) owns where it is actually found in the world; this entry only makes it a real, nameable satchel item so SD18's recipes have something to spend. `kind: resource` (same as wood/stone/fiber) rather than a new kind -- nothing branches on kind besides `tool`, so a fourth resource-shaped id needs no new code path.
_comment_ironwood: SF31. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md §3 Band 4 and §10: the SECOND and LAST of the Meadows' two progression-tier materials, above baseline wood/stone/fiber/berries and alongside Rootstone. `gathered_with: axe` because it is wood -- the spec's own note that it 'does not need to literally be iron' cuts both ways, and giving a hardwood a new gathering verb would be a mechanic where the spec asked for a tier. `kind: resource`, same as Rootstone, so no new code path. Where it grows is `data/config/harvest.json`'s `ironwood` nodes (the old-growth stands on the Rise's south-west flank, spec Band 4's 'old-growth forest'); what it buys is `data/recipes/recipes_ironwood.json`, and that file's own header holds the rule this tier is judged by: nothing the stronghold needs may require a THIRD new material.
_comment_sigils: SF34, spec §3 Band 4. Three physical items, one per regional captain, each granted through that captain's `reward` block in data/config/trainers.json. `kind: key` and `stack: 1`, exactly like `south_bridge_key` -- they are gate items, and the gate is SB10's `item_gate.gd` requiring all three at once, not a level check and not a UI lock. There is no fourth sigil and no way to buy, craft or find one: beating the captain IS the acquisition.
_comment_armor: R7.7. GAME_DESIGN.md sec18's five trainer equipment slots (Helmet, Upper body, Lower body, Boots, Backpack) -- 'trainer armor protects the human, not creatures'. `kind: "armor"` items are worn, not spent (`stack: 1`, same as a tool), and carry two fields nothing else in this file uses: `armor_slot` (one of the five slot names scripts/player/player_equipment.gd knows) and `defense` (a 0..1 fraction of incoming damage the piece alone soaks, summed across every equipped piece and capped by player_equipment.gd's own MAX_TOTAL_DEFENSE). CLAUDE.md's hard rules bound this on purpose: no shields (this is passive damage reduction, never a block/parry verb), and the human still cannot fight (nothing here is a weapon or adds an attack). The only real damage source the Meadows has today is a fall (player_vitals.gd's own fall-damage curve), so that is the one thing armor reduces so far; GAME_DESIGN.md's 'later biomes require gear' line is explicitly Biome-2 scope and stays unbuilt. Icons are original flat silhouettes (tools/gen_item_icons.py, spec sec21's sanctioned 'simple generated vector icons for game-specific concepts') -- neither vendored Kenney icon pack this project uses has a clothing/armor glyph to reuse.
_comment_saddle_frame: SD18/R6.2. An intermediate crafted component, not a gathered resource -- `kind: material` says so without inventing a branch nothing reads yet (same 'descriptive only' rule `coin`'s `kind: currency` documents). Consumed later by the Riding Saddle (R6.2, spec Band 4) once the saddle recipe itself is built; this item and the recipe that makes it are SD18's whole contribution toward that -- no riding code, no mount/dismount, nothing here reads or writes anything about a creature.

coin.name: Coin
coin.blurb: Village coin. Mira takes it, and pays it.
coin.description: Small struck coins, worn smooth at the rims from passing hand to hand around the square. Mira the merchant counts in them, and so does anyone else in the Meadows with something to sell.

wood.name: Wood
wood.blurb: Cut from the oaks. Everything early is made of it.
wood.description: Rough-cut lengths from the meadow's oaks. It is the first thing you gather and the last thing you stop needing — walls, tools and campfires all start here.

stone.name: Stone
stone.description: Hard grey chunks worked loose from an outcrop, heavier in the hand than the wood pile. Foundations and hearths want it, and a pickaxe pulls it free whole.

fiber.name: Fiber
fiber.blurb: Stripped from meadow grass. Binds and stuffs.
fiber.description: Long green strands stripped clean from meadow grass. Not much to look at alone, but bindings, stuffing and cord all lean on it.

berries.name: Berries
berries.blurb: A handful off a bush. Food buffs, never starvation.
berries.description: A cupped handful picked straight off a meadow bush, still warm from the sun. A quick bite tops up satiety and leaves a little spring in your step for a couple of minutes after.

berry_seeds.name: Berry Seeds
berry_seeds._comment: R7.6. What a farm plot is sown with (data/config/farm.json, scripts/world/farm_plot.gd). `kind: resource` like wood and fiber rather than a new `seed` kind -- nothing in item_db.gd branches on kind except `tool`, so a seed-shaped id needs no new code path, and inventing a kind nothing reads is the speculative machinery CLAUDE.md's working-style section says not to build. Never tool-gated: seeds come from a recipe (3 berries -> 4 seeds, data/recipes/recipes.json) and from Mira (data/config/trade.json), not out of the ground. The icon reuses the existing `berries` silhouette in the same honest stand-in convention `rootstone` documents below -- the set has no seed glyph, and a berry is what is in the packet.
berry_seeds.blurb: A twist of dried berries, saved for planting.
berry_seeds.description: Seed saved out of last season's picking and dried in a twist of cloth. Sown into worked ground it comes up as a bush inside a day, which is the whole of what farming is here.

rootstone.name: Rootstone
rootstone._comment: SD17. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Sec10: the FIRST of exactly two tier materials in the whole biome (Rootstone, then Ironwood) on top of wood/stone/fiber/berries. The Burrow Warrens' deposits are its first source in the world; the Old Quarry is the other, and SD18 owns every recipe that spends it -- per that item, Rootstone only ever UPGRADES something the player already has (better orb tier, workbench, gathering tool, saddle component), never opens a new tree. The icon reuses the existing `stone` silhouette on purpose: the icon set has no rootstone glyph, this is an honest stand-in in the same convention several other items already use, and it is not new asset sourcing.
rootstone.blurb: Green-veined stone from deep ground. Better than plain rock.
rootstone.description: Grey stone shot through with living green veins that keep their colour long after the block is broken out. It comes only from deep seams -- warrens, old quarry faces -- and everything made with it comes out stronger than the same thing made of ordinary rock.

ironwood.name: Ironwood
ironwood.blurb: Upper-Meadows hardwood. Dulls an ordinary axe and outlasts everything you build from it.
ironwood.description: Close-grained wood cut from the old-growth stands on the Rise's flank, so dense a fresh-cut round barely floats. It is still wood — the axe is still the tool — but it takes twice the swinging, and what it braces does not give.

orb_prime.name: Prime Orb
orb_prime.blurb: Ironwood-sprung bands. The best odds the Meadows can build.
orb_prime.description: A greater orb rebuilt around a sprung ironwood core, so the bands close harder and hold longer instead of flexing open on the first surge. The last rung of the tier ladder the Meadows has materials for.

potion_large.name: Ridge Tonic
potion_large.blurb: A proper dose, brewed from ironwood bark. For the long fights.
potion_large.description: Bitter resin boiled out of ironwood bark and cut with berry pulp. More than twice a small potion's worth in one go — the thing you carry into a gauntlet where there is no time to stop and pour three.

field_sigil.name: Field Sigil
field_sigil.blurb: The Field Captain's own. One of three that turn the Hall approach.
field_sigil.description: A heavy bronze disc struck with Team Tether's mark and the ploughed-furrow device of the high pasture posting. A captain carries one, and hands it over when they lose — the officers' own rule, and they keep it.

ridge_sigil.name: Ridge Sigil
ridge_sigil.blurb: The Ridge Captain's own. One of three that turn the Hall approach.
ridge_sigil.description: The same bronze disc, struck instead with the wind-ridge's three-peak device and worn pale along one edge by a lanyard that has spent years in a crosswind.

river_sigil.name: River Sigil
river_sigil.blurb: The Riverwatch Captain's own. One of three that turn the Hall approach.
river_sigil.description: The Riverwatch posting's disc, its device a channel running between two banks. Water-stained, and kept polished anyway.

saddle_frame.name: Saddle Frame
saddle_frame.blurb: A rootstone-braced skeleton. Wants leather and a creature's back, in that order.
saddle_frame.description: A rigid frame built to take real weight, its joints braced with worked rootstone rather than plain wood. Not a saddle yet — just the part that has to be right before the rest of one is worth building.

saddle.name: Riding Saddle
saddle.blurb: Frame, girth and stirrups. Whatever will carry you can carry you now.
saddle.description: A finished saddle: the rootstone-braced frame wrapped, padded and strapped, with a girth long enough to go round something with a deer's chest. Owning one is the whole difference between a creature that walks beside you and a creature you can get on.

orb_basic.name: Orb
orb_basic.blurb: Plain make, from Grandpa's pack. A good throw matters more than a good orb.
orb_basic.description: A plain, unmarked sphere from Grandpa's old pack — no dial, no fittings, nothing fancy. It works because your throw does the work, not the orb.

orb_greater.name: Greater Orb
orb_greater.blurb: Reinforced tether bands. Meaningfully better odds than a plain orb.
orb_greater.description: A reinforced take on the plain orb, its tether bands doubled and set tighter. A creature caught in this one has a real fight on its hands before it breaks free.

potion_small.name: Small Potion
potion_small.blurb: Patches a creature's scrapes. For your creature, mind — you get soup.
potion_small.description: A small dose that closes cuts and eases bruising on a creature fast. It only works on a creature — for you, it's soup and rest, same as always.

revive.name: Revive
revive.blurb: Brings a fainted creature back up, half strength. Nothing else does.
revive.description: A denser, costlier draught than a potion, and the only thing that raises a creature back up once it's fainted. It comes back at half its full strength — a proper rest is still what finishes the job.

axe.name: Axe
axe.blurb: Bites into oak cleanly. Bare hands barely dent it.
axe.description: A proper woodcutter's edge. It takes a full swing off an oak in the time bare hands would still be scraping bark, and it wears down a little with every tree.

pickaxe.name: Pickaxe
pickaxe.blurb: Cracks stone loose whole. Bare hands just bruise.
pickaxe.description: Heavy-headed and built for outcrops. It cracks a full block of stone loose in one go where bare hands would only bruise a knuckle against it.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.blurb: For the workbench, not the woods. Free repairs start here.
hammer.description: A workbench tool, not a woodcutting one. Bring a worn-out tool to the bench with this in hand and the repair costs nothing but time.

knife.name: Knife
knife.blurb: Strips fiber in one clean pull.
knife.description: Short, sharp, and built for stripping — one clean pull takes fiber off meadow grass that bare hands would only tear at unevenly.

hoe.name: Hoe
hoe._comment: R7.6. The SIXTH tool, and the first that gates something other than a gather: it turns unworked ground into a seedbed (scripts/world/farm_logic.gd::TILL_TOOL) and does nothing else. It deliberately appears in NO item's `gathered_with` -- see docs/decisions/D50 and this file's own `_comment_tools` line, which records berries as the one resource that is never tool-gated. That stayed true: farmed berries are picked bare-handed exactly like wild ones. `durability` matches the other five, and D50's 'harvest returns the bed to TILLED' rule is what keeps a 40-charge hoe from being a permanent tax -- six beds cost six charges once, not six per crop.
hoe._comment_model: `held_model` and `icon` both reuse the bronze pickaxe. There is no hoe mesh and no hoe glyph in any vendored pack, and D24 forbids sourcing a new prop family for one tool; a bronze mattock head on a shaft is what a hoe looks like at hand scale, and this is the same honest stand-in `hammer` above already makes with the survival pack's axe. Held a little flatter than the pickaxe (-45 rather than -15 on roll) so the two read apart in the hand.
hoe.blurb: Breaks ground into a seedbed. Nothing else.
hoe.description: A broad flat blade on a long shaft, for turning matted meadow sod into soil loose enough to take seed. It is no use on a tree, a rock or a creature — the only thing it is for is the ground in front of a farmhouse.

fishing_rod.name: Fishing Rod
fishing_rod.blurb: For water that doesn't exist yet.
fishing_rod.description: A proper rod and line, ready the moment there's water worth casting into. For now it just rides in the satchel, waiting.

torch.name: Torch
torch.blurb: Pull it from the pack and it lights your way.
torch.description: A pitch-soaked stick, ready to strike. Draw it from the satchel like any other tool and it rides lit in the trainer's hand -- on its own once night falls, or sooner with a press.

tm_stone_rush.name: TM: Stone Rush
tm_stone_rush.blurb: A teaching disc. One creature, one lesson.
tm_stone_rush.description: A flat grey disc that hums faintly when a ground-type creature is near. Hold it out and the creature takes the shape of the move straight off it — once. The disc goes dull afterwards.

tm_burrow_strike.name: TM: Burrow Strike
tm_burrow_strike.blurb: A teaching disc. One creature, one lesson.
tm_burrow_strike.description: Earth-brown and gritty to the touch, this one carries the trick of coming up underneath something instead of at it. A ground-type creature learns it in a single sitting, and the disc is spent.

castle_gate_key.name: Old Key
castle_gate_key.blurb: Heavy and old. Something nearby is still locked.
castle_gate_key.description: Iron gone dark with age, too heavy for the small lock it probably once fit. Something nearby is still shut tight, and this is the only thing you own that might open it.

south_bridge_key.name: South Bridge Key
south_bridge_key.blurb: Oskar's own. Turns the old crossing south of the village.
south_bridge_key.description: Plain iron, kept oiled and working rather than decorative -- a bridgehand's tool, not a keepsake. Oskar hands it over the moment he loses fair, square terms he was plain about from the start. It turns the mechanism at the old south bridge.

heartstone.name: Heartstone
heartstone._comment: SD17 / R4.6. The evolution catalyst the evolution gate was built for and then left switched off waiting on -- see data/config/progression.json's `_comment_evolution`, which named this exact item and this exact backlog entry a phase in advance. `evolution.mudsnout.item_id` is now `heartstone`, and the one in the world sits in the Burrow Warrens' branch chamber behind the guardian. `stack: 1` because there is exactly one, and consuming it in an evolution is what removes it from play. Same honest icon stand-in as `rootstone` above.
heartstone.blurb: Warm to hold, and beating slowly.
heartstone.description: A dark red stone the size of a fist, warm in a way stone should not be, with a slow pulse somewhere under the surface. A creature held close to one has been known to finish becoming whatever it was already turning into.

sunstone.name: Sunstone
sunstone._comment: D71/T3-SUNSTONE. The second Mudsnout evolution catalyst, mirroring `heartstone` above in every way that isn't the point of it being a DIFFERENT stone -- same `kind`/`stack`/icon convention, same one-time physical pickup (scripts/world/key_pickup.gd), same consuming role in scripts/creatures/evolution.gd::evolve(). Read by species.json's `mudsnout.evolves_into_variants` (item_id -> target), not by progression.json's `evolution.mudsnout` block -- that block still only names the Heartstone path, deliberately, so the Sunstone branch is pure addition (see ralph/reports/SUNSTONE_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md). The one in the world sits in the scorched Team Tether industrial ground by the Sigil gate (band 5), the same pocket that held T3-CREATURES's now-removed wild Ashtusk individual -- see data/config/bands/band5_stronghold_approach/spawns.json's `_comment_ashtusk_removed`. `stack: 1` for the same reason as Heartstone: there is exactly one, and evolving with it is what removes it from play. Same honest icon stand-in as `stone`/`rootstone`/`heartstone`.
sunstone.blurb: Hot to hold, and smelling faintly of ash.
sunstone.description: A dark, glassy stone shot through with veins of orange light, warm enough to feel through a glove even before you close your hand around it. A creature held close to one does not simply grow -- it changes, the way stone changes when it has spent long enough near real heat.

mill_bridge_gear._comment: SE27, and SB10's Gate 2 (SE22's Old Mill Crossing). Added here by SE27 because the rescue that hands it over needs a real item to hand over; SE22 is building the crossing that reads it. IF A SIBLING TASK ALSO ADDED THIS ID, THE TWO ENTRIES ARE A DUPLICATE TO RESOLVE AT MERGE -- keep one, and keep whichever `icon` path actually has a PNG behind it (this one is generated by tools/gen_item_icons.py::icon_mill_bridge_gear).
mill_bridge_gear.name: Mill Bridge Gear
mill_bridge_gear.blurb: The drive gear out of the mill crossing. Team Tether took it; you took it back.
mill_bridge_gear.description: A machined bronze cog, heavier than it looks, with a keyway cut through the bore for the shaft it seats on. Team Tether did not break the Old Mill Crossing -- they simply removed the one part that made it work, and then removed the one person who knew where it went. Refitted, the crossing works again, for good.

tm_rock_throw.name: TM: Rock Throw
tm_rock_throw.blurb: A heavier stone, thrown harder and further than a pebble.
tm_rock_throw.description: A heavier stone, thrown harder and further than a pebble. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's quick slot.

tm_stone_spike.name: TM: Stone Spike
tm_stone_spike.blurb: A ridge of stone erupts along the ground ahead of you.
tm_stone_spike.description: A ridge of stone erupts along the ground ahead of you. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_earth_fist.name: TM: Earth Fist
tm_earth_fist.blurb: A committed blow that carries a shockwave through the ground.
tm_earth_fist.description: A committed blow that carries a shockwave through the ground. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_earthshatter.name: TM: Earthshatter
tm_earthshatter.blurb: The ground itself comes apart. Very rare, and it ends fights.
tm_earthshatter.description: The ground itself comes apart. Very rare, and it ends fights. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_aqua_shot.name: TM: Aqua Shot
tm_aqua_shot.blurb: A fast bolt of pressurised water. Reaches where a jab cannot.
tm_aqua_shot.description: A fast bolt of pressurised water. Reaches where a jab cannot. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's quick slot.

tm_tidal_burst.name: TM: Tidal Burst
tm_tidal_burst.blurb: A short wave that washes over everything in front of it.
tm_tidal_burst.description: A short wave that washes over everything in front of it. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_riptide_lance.name: TM: Riptide Lance
tm_riptide_lance.blurb: A single focused spear of water, thrown the length of the arena.
tm_riptide_lance.description: A single focused spear of water, thrown the length of the arena. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_leviathan_surge.name: TM: Leviathan Surge
tm_leviathan_surge.blurb: Something vast moves through the water ahead of you. Very rare.
tm_leviathan_surge.description: Something vast moves through the water ahead of you. Very rare. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_wind_blade.name: TM: Wind Blade
tm_wind_blade.blurb: A visible cutting edge of compressed air.
tm_wind_blade.description: A visible cutting edge of compressed air. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's quick slot.

tm_aerial_flash.name: TM: Aerial Flash
tm_aerial_flash.blurb: A dash so fast the strike lands before the movement reads.
tm_aerial_flash.description: A dash so fast the strike lands before the movement reads. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_cyclone.name: TM: Cyclone
tm_cyclone.blurb: A turning column of wind that stays where you put it.
tm_cyclone.description: A turning column of wind that stays where you put it. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

tm_heavenfall.name: TM: Heavenfall
tm_heavenfall.blurb: Everything the sky has, at once. Very rare.
tm_heavenfall.description: Everything the sky has, at once. Very rare. Teaching it spends the disc, and it replaces whatever sits in that creature's charged slot.

elixir_might.name: Elixir of Might
elixir_might.blurb: Permanent. Raises one creature's attack, for good.
elixir_might.description: Thick and slow-pouring, and it tastes of hot iron. A creature that drinks one hits harder for the rest of its life -- there is no wearing off and no drinking it back. Rare enough that choosing WHO drinks it is most of the decision.

elixir_guard.name: Elixir of Guard
elixir_guard.blurb: Permanent. Raises one creature's defence, for good.
elixir_guard.description: Settles into a grey sheen if it stands too long, and has to be shaken before it will pour. What it puts into a creature stays there: a permanent thickening of hide, shell or feather that no amount of resting undoes.

elixir_vigour.name: Elixir of Vigour
elixir_vigour.blurb: Permanent. Raises one creature's maximum health, for good.
elixir_vigour.description: Green, and it smells like the meadow after rain. It raises the ceiling rather than filling the cup -- a creature drinks one and can hold more from then on, but walks away no more healed than it was.

swift_tonic.name: Swift Tonic
swift_tonic.blurb: Temporary. Your creature moves faster, for a couple of minutes.
swift_tonic.description: Bright and fizzing, and it goes to the legs. The creature that drinks it circles faster, closes faster and disengages faster for about two minutes -- then it is gone, and so is the edge.

attack_tonic.name: Attack Tonic
attack_tonic.blurb: Temporary. Your creature hits harder, for a minute and a half.
attack_tonic.description: Tastes of iron filings and dares. Every blow the drinker lands for the next minute and a half carries extra weight; when it fades, it fades completely. Drink it for the fight in front of you, not the one you might meet.

stoneguard_brew.name: Stoneguard Brew
stoneguard_brew.blurb: Temporary. Your creature takes hits better, for a minute and a half.
stoneguard_brew.description: Grey, gritty, and it settles the nerves like a wall settles wind. Hide and feather sit heavier on the drinker for a minute and a half -- long enough for one hard fight, never long enough to live behind.

hide_helm.name: Hide Helm
hide_helm.blurb: Boiled hide over the crown. Takes the edge off a bad fall.
hide_helm.description: Stiffened hide, shaped over a form and left to dry hard. It will not stop a real blow -- nothing here is meant to, the trainer never fights -- but a knock on the head from a bad landing lands softer wearing it.

hide_vest.name: Hide Vest
hide_vest.blurb: Layered hide over the chest and back. The biggest piece of the set.
hide_vest.description: Two layers of hide laced over the ribs and shoulder blades, the largest single piece a trainer can wear and the one that does the most against a fall's own jolt.

hide_leggings.name: Hide Leggings
hide_leggings.blurb: Hide wrapped over the thighs and knees.
hide_leggings.description: Wrapped and buckled over the thighs and knees, the joints that take the worst of a hard landing on uneven ground.

hide_boots.name: Hide Boots
hide_boots.blurb: Thick-soled hide boots. Softer on the ankles than bare feet.
hide_boots.description: Thick-soled and double-stitched at the ankle. Not built for speed -- built so the ground stops being the first thing you feel when you land wrong.

travel_pack.name: Travel Pack
travel_pack.blurb: A padded frame pack. Takes a little sting out of landing on your back.
travel_pack.description: A padded frame worn high on the back. It carries nothing the satchel does not already hold -- CLAUDE.md's own rule against a carry-weight system stands -- but the padding softens a landing taken square on the spine.

_comment_held: Tools carry the mesh they appear in the trainer's hand as. Owner playtest: "the tools exist but you can't pull them out when you're exploring and use them" -- before this a tool was an inventory row and nothing else, and pressing it on the hotbar only repaired it. `scripts/player/tool_hold.gd` bone-attaches `held_model` to the trainer's hand, using the same BoneAttachment3D pattern the carried torch already uses (scripts/player/torch.gd). `held_offset`/`held_rotation_deg` are the fit in that hand and are TUNABLE. An empty `held_model` means the tool is carried but never drawn -- fishing_rod, which has no water to fish yet and no vendored rod mesh (D24: no new asset families for one prop).
_comment_torch: OW12 (owner, 2026-08-16: 'torches need to be a carry able item not placeable one'), which supersedes OF24's placeable torch (see data/items/buildables.json's own retirement note) and OF24's earlier always-on kit torch (scripts/player/torch.gd used to build and attach it unconditionally at spawn, no item required). The torch is now `kind: "tool"` like axe/pickaxe/knife -- equipped off the hotbar/backpack the same way, `held_model`/`held_offset`/`held_rotation_deg` reaching the hand through tool_hold.gd's existing generic mechanism rather than a second hand-attachment system. `scripts/player/torch.gd` now owns only the light (the forward-throw SpotLight and the prop's own flickering OmniLight) and stays dark, whatever the hour, unless the torch is the equipped tool -- an unequipped torch is an inert satchel row, same as an unequipped axe. `icon` reuses the existing build-menu torch silhouette (assets/ui/icons/buildables/torch.png) rather than sourcing a new one -- same honest-stand-in convention rootstone/heartstone already use, and D24 forbids a fresh asset for one prop anyway. No `durability`: it gathers nothing, so nothing here wears it down. See docs/decisions/D53 for the full reasoning, including the one gap this task deliberately did not invent a fix for (camp lighting at night, now stranded with the placeable retired).
_comment_elixirs: D47. `kind: "elixir"` is a PERMANENT stat gain spent on one creature, and it is the one thing in this file that is not reversible -- every other consumable heals, feeds or revives. `elixir_stat` is hp/attack/defence and `elixir_points` is raw stat points, capped per creature by data/config/progression.json's `elixirs.cap_per_stat`. They deliberately do NOT appear in Mira's stock (data/config/trade.json): the owner asked for permanent boosters to stay rare, and anything purchasable is only as rare as your coin pile. They belong in the world -- a dungeon, a captain, a stronghold. They share the potion icon for now rather than blocking on new art (D24: no new asset family for three items); tools/gen_item_icons.py is where a bespoke one would go.
_comment_saddle: R6.2. ONE generic saddle for every mount, never a saddle per species — the backlog brief's own words, 'a generic saddle ... and no species-specific saddle clutter'. Which creature it fits is the CREATURE's business (species.json's `rideable.requires_item`), so a second mount at R8.5 either wants this same saddle or names its own tack there, and either way nothing changes here. `kind: gear` rather than `material`: it is a thing you own and use, like an orb, not a thing you spend. It is never consumed by riding and there is no durability on it — `scripts/world/riding_controller.gd::_has_tack()` only ever ASKS whether one is in the satchel. Icon deliberately points at `saddle_frame.png`: the frame is what a saddle is built on and the silhouette is right, and CLAUDE.md's asset rules say to source coherently rather than mint a near-duplicate icon for the sake of a distinct filename. A dedicated icon is a clean later swap in this one line. [Moved out of the `items` object: every other entry in there is an item dictionary, and tests/test_item_icons.gd casts each one, so a bare string inside it threw a cast error on three separate tests. Top level is where every other _comment in this file already sits.]
_comment_tonics: The potions board's TEMPORARY half (the permanent half is D47's elixirs). A `creature_buff` block is a timed multiplier on ONE creature stat -- applied through creature_instance.gd::apply_buff, ticked down by GameState._process, multiplied into effective_attack/effective_defence (or the combat drive speed), and gone when the clock runs out. Re-drinking refreshes the clock, never stacks the multiplier -- the owner's brief forbade mandatory buff maintenance and stacking is how that ritual is born. NOT saved: a timed buff dying on quit is the honest reading of temporary. Sold by Mira at modest prices -- tonics are the RENEWABLE economy hook, elixirs stay unsold and rare. Board names where the board had them (Swift Tonic, Stoneguard Brew). They share the potion icon for now (D24: no new asset family for three items).
_comment_t3_activities_board_audit: T3-ACTIVITIES, closing two findings T3-PICKUPS's handover (2026-08-30) flagged rather than resolved. RE-VERIFIED FIRST, against the live tree rather than trusting the handover's own numbers (per this repo's own 'evidence-backed already fixed is valid' rule): every one of the three elixirs (elixir_might/guard/vigour, all now placed via T3-PICKUPS's item_cache_pickup.gd and T3-REWARD's three captain rewards) and all five armor pieces (hide_helm/vest/leggings/boots, travel_pack, split across T3-REWARD's Warrens reward and T3-PICKUPS's harvest-node scatter) has a real acquisition path today. A repo-wide id-presence scan (band harvest/trainers/props, burrow_warrens.json, trade.json, dialogue) turned up exactly two other item ids with no reference anywhere: `fishing_rod`, whose own blurb already says why ('for water that doesn't exist yet' -- no fishing verb is built, so this is not a bug); and `saddle_frame`, which IS reachable, through `data/recipes/recipes_rootstone.json`'s own recipe -- the scan's file list had simply missed `data/recipes/`. Nothing in the reward ladder is orphaned as of this branch. DECISIONS on the two remaining board findings, made explicitly rather than left silent: (1) the owner board's 'Defense Elixir' appearing in BOTH the PERMANENT and TEMPORARY columns is a labelling duplicate in the board's own concept art, not two items -- `elixir_guard` (permanent) and `stoneguard_brew` (temporary) already cover both real niches the two labels could mean, and nothing further is invented. (2) 'Clarity Draught' stays UNBUILT, on purpose, not merely unimplemented: the temporary tonic row already has one tonic per stat this codebase can actually buff (speed/swift_tonic, attack/attack_tonic, defence/stoneguard_brew -- `creature_instance.gd`'s buff plumbing has no fourth hook), so a Clarity Draught would need either a genuinely new buffable axis (accuracy, catch-chance, status-cure) or a fourth reskin of a stat the board already names elsewhere. The former is a combat-mechanics change on the scale CLAUDE.md's own ask-list reserves for the owner ('changing the type system' is the nearest precedent for 'adding a new kind of buff'), not a reward-routing task's to invent; the latter would not be a real item, only a fourth name for one of the first three. Left for whoever next owns new item/buff design, with the two candidate readings named above so they do not have to be rediscovered.
